title: 35th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with routine business, a moment of silence for a former Faafu Atoll member, and a referral of the President's nominee for ambassador to Saudi Arabia to the Foreign Relations Committee. Most of the part was the preliminary debate on a government bill raising the tourism GST from 16% to 17% from June 2025, with members from the governing side backing it as needed revenue and opposition and some other members questioning consultation, spending and past promises. The debate closed and the bill goes to a vote at voting time; debate on a separate airport tax and fee bill had just begun when this part ends. The text is heavily garbled in places, so some positions are only broadly captured. Members spent the sitting debating the government's bill to raise the departure tax and airport fees paid by passengers leaving the Maldives (Law 29/2016), discussed together with the GST and Tourism Act amendment bills. Government-side members said the money is needed for airport development, debt repayment and a stronger Sovereign Development Fund, and that economy-class Maldivians are not affected. Opposition members questioned the lack of a cost estimate and consultation with tourism businesses, and the effect on tourist numbers. The GST Act (10/2011) amendment bill was accepted 52-7 and sent to the Committee of the Whole House; the departure tax debate was not finished and continues on 16 October. Some of the text is garbled, so speaker gists are approximate.

items.title: Bill to amend the Goods and Services Tax Act (Law 10/2011), submitted for the government by the member for West Maafannu
items.outcome: accepted 52-7 and sent to the Committee of the Whole House as a tax bill

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Backed the bill, citing past GST and TGST increases and large unpaid state bills to health and construction firms; asked committee to look at resort staff outlets.
Said critics misrepresent the bill as a tax on citizens and that the revenue is needed.
Supported the amendment, saying airport fees help repay airport loans and rebuild the Sovereign Development Fund.
Disputed opposition claims about the past government's finances.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Introduced the bill: tourism GST up one point, with projected extra revenue of MVR 201.9m in 2025, 330.8m in 2026 and 530.4m in 2027.
In closing, said the rise falls on tourism rather than citizens' pockets and urged members to support it.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the bill conflicts with the President's campaign pledge not to raise taxes and criticised the 'tax base' explanation.
Said the government had promised not to raise taxes and questioned how well the bill was studied.
Argued it would hurt tourism and asked for Gan and Hanimaadhoo airport passengers to be exempted.
Said he does not support the bill.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, saying extra revenue can fund health, education and infrastructure, and criticised the previous government.
Supported the bill, saying it funds airport infrastructure and will not harm ordinary citizens.
Noted it sets a principle for refunding fees collected wrongly from passengers.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, calling a one point rise small given the economy's state; also urged help for small businesses and recovery of stolen funds.
Supported the bill, saying the rises fall mainly on business and higher-class travellers.
Urged the committee stage to consult stakeholders and improve the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the amendment, saying a one point rise has little effect on ordinary Maldivians, and blamed past debt and borrowing for the current situation.
Supported the bill, saying the government is also cutting costs and the money goes to debt repayment.
Said private jet and VIP passengers elsewhere pay comparable or higher charges.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the amendment but warned that combined TGST, green tax and airport charges burden small guesthouses and mid-sized businesses; urged consultation.
Said he would back the government on the taxes and vote for the bill.
Raised concern that no development project had run in his constituency's islands in a year and urged consulting industry experts.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said he could back tax changes if stakeholders are properly consulted, questioned the President's earlier statements and sudden policy changes, and raised stalled island water and sewerage works.
Said finance-related bills are being submitted suddenly and that tour operators and travel agents were not properly consulted.
Warned higher ticket costs could reduce tourist arrivals, especially at guesthouses.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the bill, saying the economy depends on tourism and the government inherited weak finances, and criticised past political appointments.
Said tax rises have been repeated by successive governments while deficits and debt keep growing.
Argued state spending, including on former officials, should be reviewed alongside revenue.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said tax changes can be justified but asked why, called for consultation, and criticised government spending, ministry numbers and stalled projects.
Said the bill came without a cost estimate or impact study and that businesses were not consulted.
Said he supports taxes in principle but not rises of up to 300 percent without visible revenue accounting.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said tourism revenue is already rising and argued the government should cut spending, political posts and corruption and restart stalled island projects.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said his main concern is the government's planning and lack of consultation, citing recent reversed decisions, and asked stakeholders be consulted.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Supported the bill overall and suggested zone-based tourism taxes, higher in the Malé area, plus a capital gains tax on resort sales.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the bill, citing a World Bank growth forecast and the government's large debt repayments, and said the rise affects tourists, not citizens.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill, saying it is a tourist tax that will not burden citizens, and criticised the previous government's job handouts and debt.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Supported the bill, saying the one point rise targets those who profit most from natural resources, and rejected opposition claims as misleading.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Began introducing his bill on taxes and fees for passengers departing from Maldivian airports.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said the fee rises are steep for tourism and questioned the state of government finances, reserves and the Sovereign Development Fund.
Said he was hesitant to vote for the bill.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill as an amendment that has to be passed, citing rising tourist arrivals this year.
Said extra revenue is needed to finish airport development.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, saying the government inherited weak finances and needs revenue to develop the airport.
Asked members not to mislead the public about the impact.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Supported the bill, saying it would bring the state about 1.7 billion rufiyaa in 2025 for development.
Asked for entry and supervisor tourism jobs to be set aside for Maldivians.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the bill, saying airport charges fund a proper terminal and are charged in many other countries.
Said economy-class Maldivian travellers would not carry a heavier burden.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill, saying the charge is paid by departing foreign visitors, not local citizens.
Asked for the committee to finish quickly.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill, pointing to national debt above 100 percent of GDP and the need to repay loans.
Said economy-class Maldivians are not burdened and criticised the opposition's arguments.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said revenue has already risen by billions of rufiyaa, so the problem is managing spending, not income.
Criticised spending on political posts and projects, and asked what happened to three earlier fiscal bills.
Called on the government to use extra revenue well.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Supported the bill, saying the government inherited heavy debt and is cutting spending, including 200 political appointees.
Asked for some relief for regional airports such as Addu's.

decisions: Minutes of the first to third special sittings were accepted as there were no amendments.
Chair announced condolences and a moment of silence for former member Abdul Ghafoor Ibrahim.
President's nomination of Ahmed Sareer as ambassador to Saudi Arabia was referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Preliminary debate on the GST amendment bill (tourism GST 16% to 17%) concluded, with the vote left for voting time.
No member asked for a third turn on the GST bill debate.
Preliminary debate on the Airports Act amendment bill (item 7.2) started.
The GST Act (10/2011) amendment bill was accepted and sent to the Committee of the Whole House because it is a tax bill.
Debate on the departure tax bill (Law 29/2016) was adjourned to the next sitting, Wednesday 16 October 2024 at 9:00.
The sitting recessed around midday and resumed at 1:00 pm.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to amend the Goods and Services Tax Act (Law 10/2011) for consideration
